Disclosure Controls and Procedures Our principal executive officer and our principal financial officer have concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the Exchange Act)) were effective as of November 2, 2025, based on the evaluation of these controls and procedures required by Rule 13a-15(b) or 15d-15(b) of the Exchange Act. Management’s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting Management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting. Our internal control system was designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the preparation and fair presentation of published financial statements in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles. All internal control systems, no matter how well designed, have inherent limitations. Therefore, even those systems determined to be effective can provide only reasonable assurance with respect to financial statement preparation and presentation in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. Management assessed the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of November 2, 2025, using the criteria set forth in Internal Control – Integrated Framework (2013) issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission. Based on that assessment, management concluded that, as of November 2, 2025, our internal control over financial reporting was effective. Our independent registered public accounting firm has issued an audit report on the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting. That report is included herein. Changes in Internal Control Over Financial Reporting During the fourth quarter of 2025, there were no changes that have materially affected or are reasonably likely to materially affect our internal control over financial reporting. This Annual Report on Form 10-K contains forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. All statements other than statements of historical fact included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K are forward-looking statements. Forward-looking statements provide our current expectations and projections relating to our financial condition, results of operations, plans, objectives, future performance, and business. You can identify forward-looking statements as they do not relate to historical or current facts and by words such as “believe,” “expect,” “estimate,” “anticipate,” “will,” “aim,” “should,” “plan,” “forecast,” “target,” “guide,” “project,” “intend,” “could,” and similar words or expressions. All forward-looking statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that may cause actual results to differ materially from those that we expected. Important factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from our expectations, or cautionary statements, and other important information about forward-looking statements are disclosed under Item 1A, “Risk Factors,” and Item 7, “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations–Forward-Looking Statements,” in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. As used herein, the terms “John Deere,” “we,” “us,” “our,” or “the Company” refer collectively to Deere & Company and its subsidiaries, unless designated or identified otherwise. All amounts are presented in millions of U.S. dollars, unless otherwise specified. Products John Deere has manufactured agricultural equipment since 1837. Deere & Company was incorporated under the laws of Delaware in 1958. Our business is managed through the following four business segments: Production & Precision Agriculture (PPA), Small Agriculture & Turf (SAT), Construction & Forestry (CF), and Financial Services (John Deere Financial or FS).

credit_strengths.text: Deere's balance sheet carries net cash, with unrestricted cash exceeding itemized interest-bearing debt, and net leverage sits far below the sector median and improved year over year. This net-cash position underpins a minimal indicative financial risk profile and gives the issuer substantial headroom against cyclical downturns in farm equipment demand.

Operating margin expanded year over year and stands well above the Industrials sector median, reflecting pricing discipline and mix in Production & Precision Agriculture despite falling revenue. Operating income recovered modestly even as the top line declined across the three-year trend, evidencing cost control through the downcycle.

key_risks.text: Revenue has declined for consecutive years as agricultural equipment demand normalizes from peak levels, and the filing flags forward-looking statements subject to risks in Risk Factors and MD&A. A prolonged farm-income downturn would pressure volumes and pricing, narrowing the margin cushion that currently supports the credit profile.

Interest coverage improved year over year but remains well below the sector median, and EBITDA coverage is likewise roughly a third of the peer benchmark. The gap reflects captive finance funding costs embedded in consolidated interest expense, so coverage metrics understate industrial-segment debt service but still constrain headroom.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Free cash flow covers dividends and buybacks more than twice over, and operating cash flow also exceeds the combined distributions, so shareholder returns are comfortably funded from internally generated cash. Capital expenditure remains modest relative to operating cash flow, leaving retained capacity for debt reduction or opportunistic investment.

Free cash flow to debt and operating cash flow to debt both exceed the sector median by a wide margin and improved year over year, indicating strong cash-based debt service capacity. Reported debt maturities are concentrated in the near years, but the net-cash position and recurring cash generation support refinancing.

overall_credit_view.text: Deere presents a strong industrial credit: net cash, leverage far below the sector median, and cash conversion well ahead of peers. The indicative financial risk profile is minimal. Our judgement is that the principal sensitivity is the agricultural cycle rather than the capital structure, given declining revenue and below-median interest coverage.

We view liquidity as adequate: cash exceeds itemized debt, free cash flow is robust, and distributions are well covered. The itemized debt tag is partial and current assets and liabilities are untagged, so working-capital liquidity cannot be measured; this gap is material but does not alter the net-cash conclusion.

credit_strengths.text: Deere 的資產負債表持有淨現金，未受限現金超過逐項列示的計息債務，而淨槓桿遠低於行業中位數並按年改善。此淨現金狀況支撐極低的指示性財務風險狀況，並賦予發行人充裕的緩衝空間以抵禦農機設備需求的週期性下滑。
營業利潤率按年擴大，並遠高於工業行業中位數，反映儘管收入下降，生產與精準農業業務仍保持定價紀律及產品組合。即使三年趨勢中收入下滑，營業利潤仍溫和回升，顯示下行週期中的成本控制。

key_risks.text: 隨著農機設備需求從高峰水平正常化，收入已連續數年下降，而申報文件標明前瞻性陳述受風險因素及管理層討論與分析中的風險所限。農業收入長期下滑將對銷量及定價構成壓力，收窄目前支撐信用狀況的利潤率緩衝。
利息覆蓋率按年改善，但仍遠低於行業中位數，而 EBITDA 覆蓋率同樣約為同業基準的三分之一。該差距反映綜合利息支出中嵌入的專屬金融融資成本，因此覆蓋率指標低估了工業分部的債務償付能力，但仍限制緩衝空間。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 自由現金流覆蓋股息及回購超過兩倍，而經營現金流亦超過合計分派，因此股東回報由內部產生現金充裕支持。資本開支相對經營現金流仍屬溫和，保留能力用於減債或機會性投資。
自由現金流對債務及經營現金流對債務均大幅超過行業中位數並按年改善，顯示強勁的現金基礎債務償付能力。呈報債務到期集中於近數年，但淨現金狀況及經常性現金產生支持再融資。

overall_credit_view.text: Deere 呈現強勁的工業信用：淨現金、槓桿遠低於行業中位數，以及現金轉換遠勝同業。指示性財務風險狀況為極低。我們的判斷是，鑑於收入下降及利息覆蓋率低於中位數，主要敏感因素為農業週期而非資本結構。
我們認為流動性充足：現金超過逐項列示債務，自由現金流穩健，而分派獲充分覆蓋。逐項列示債務標籤屬部分性質，且流動資產及負債未標籤，因此無法衡量營運資金流動性；此缺口屬重大，但不改變淨現金結論。
